`migration_v1.json` is a synthetic reference for the R3 module extraction.
No market observations are included. `migration_cases.py` defines every input.
The JSON records SHA256 provenance for the original Python implementations.

The reference was generated by parsing those original files, compiling only
the named numerical functions into isolated namespaces with their frozen
configuration values, and executing them on the synthetic cases. Experiment
registries, entry points, market partitions and preservation runners were
never imported. The pre-refactor flat files were copied outside the repository
before editing; the experiment implementations remain in their original paths.

Coverage includes all 26 feature values at ten boundary/gap origins, all 900
first-passage records, exact risk-trial keys/responses, the original 80-round
tree's cuts/loss history/hazards, complete matched/coarse logistic coefficients,
KM and reverse-censor curves, IPCW weights, Platt coefficients, empirical and
rolling controls, calendar uncertainty, risk metrics, exposure, and every cash
increment of the synthetic execution case. The original slow He accountant
was also reconciled with the original optimized accountant before freezing.

These are migration fixtures, not proof that a research experiment can be
rerun against old receipts after its source bytes have changed. Exact archived
reproduction requires the original code/environment and original artifacts.
